note: Data-driven focus areas, role codes, and coordination channels. scripts/coord reads this so the Product Owner can redesign the area set WITHOUT a code change (docs/ORGANISATION.md section 9). If this file is missing or corrupt, coord falls back to its built-in defaults (the same eleven areas and sm_owned set) so coordination never breaks. Keep docs/FOCUS_AREAS.md in sync; a change here is a rules change (two peer reviews, or the sole-account self-review).

agent_name.note: A role is a 2-letter area code (below) for a worker, or 'sm' / 'po' for the process roles. <n> is a positive integer, unique per (role, host) and NEVER reused: a replacement worker is a new entity with a new number. Host is lowercase.

channels.sm: Scrum master <-> scrum master handoff (one SM per computer).
channels.po: Product owner <-> product owner handoff (one PO per computer).
channels.takeover: Takeover requests: a live agent asks the fleet to take over an area whose holder has gone quiet.

message.note: Direct agent-to-agent messages, addressed to ONE named agent (refs/coord/msg/<agent>). The generated initial prompt starts a worker; after that, agents talk to each other directly with `coord msg` / `coord inbox` instead of routing through the human. Append-only, like a note; never a lock.

sm_owned_note: The Scrum Master's ONE lane: the process docs themselves (`rules`). The SM is a process role that organises the fleet, so its only focus area is the coordination rules; everything that makes or ships the game - including `platform` (build/CI/scripts/packaging) - is a normal WORKER lane. The SM is never routed to game or build work: `coord next` offers an SM only an sm_owned area, and falls through to its durable jobs (drain the merge queue, review) when that lane is held. The PO never schedules the SM's lane. See ADR-0041: the SM must not do project work (human directive 2026-10-17).
